summary: Cloudflare R2 migration backend verified end-to-end. All 13/13 pytest cases PASS. POST /api/upload returns a public https R2 URL (pub-*.r2.dev) that is reachable and returns image/jpeg content, and correctly rejects non-image (415) and empty (400). POST /api/events with a base64 data-URI stores the photo as an https R2 URL in the DB and never returns raw base64 in the response (isApproved=false as expected for user-submitted events). PUT /api/events/{id} with a base64 photo also normalizes to an R2 URL. GET /api/events (list) and GET /api/events/{id} (detail) contain ZERO base64 blobs — every photos[] entry is an http(s) URL and payload size is well under 5MB. GET /api/events/{id}/photo/{i}/image.jpg always returns image/jpeg (serves a gray placeholder gracefully for invalid id / out-of-range index / non-base64 content). Startup indexes created successfully: admin login (admin@okcarevents.com / admin123) returns 200 with isAdmin=true, confirming the users.email index did not break auth. Health endpoint is healthy and reports db=connected. No frontend testing requested; backend only.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/storage.py normalize_photo is correctly fail-safe: on R2 upload failure the original value is kept, which preserves write availability. event_helper's _event_photo_urls then suppresses raw base64 from reads by rewriting to /api/events/{id}/photo/{i}/image.jpg. Combined, this guarantees reads NEVER leak base64 even if the R2 upload path transiently fails. Good defensive design.

backend/routes/media.py reads the entire upload into memory before size-checking (await file.read() then len > MAX_BYTES). For large uploads (>15MB) this still allocates the full buffer before returning 413. Low priority — Starlette caps request bodies at the ingress layer, and the limit is only 15MB.
backend/routes/events.py:_base_url treats any non-local x-forwarded-host as safe and uses x-forwarded-proto. Looks correct for the k8s ingress setup.
backend/server.py ensure_indexes uses background=True for every index and swallows exceptions — safe for repeated boots; admin login still succeeds post-startup (verified).

backend/.env uses R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://pub-ab600a60556342dcb417c5b01147968b.r2.dev — this is correctly the public R2 subdomain, so URLs returned to clients are CDN-served and never hit the backend. Verified by fetching one in-test and getting HTTP 200 + image/jpeg.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_r2_migration.py (NEW — 13 pytest cases covering the full R2 migration spec)
seed_data_creation: Each test run creates ~4 TEST_R2_* events via POST /api/events (title prefixed 'TEST_R2_Event_<hex>' / 'TEST_R2_ManualVerify') and auto-cleans them via DELETE in the created_event_ids fixture teardown. Uploads to R2 generate hashed object keys under streetmotion/<uuid>.jpg — these persist in the bucket but are harmless (immutable, cache-controlled); the per-process _hash_cache dedupes identical bytes within a worker.
context_for_next_testing_agent: R2 migration is fully working. Reusable regression suite: /app/backend/tests/test_r2_migration.py — run with `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_r2_migration.py -v`. Uses EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL (fallback to the preview URL). The test file auto-creates and auto-deletes its test events. If R2 ever misconfigures, upload_data_uri will return None and normalize_photo falls back to keeping the original base64 — in that case the test_create_event_converts_base64_to_r2_url test will fail with a 'data:' URL in photos[0], which is the correct canary.
